unmapped_findings: Product of strength and ductility of the 850 °C annealed specimen is 19 GPa% (Table 1).
Lattice parameters from XRD of the annealed specimens: α phase 2.89–2.91 Å, γ phase 3.65–3.67 Å, κ-carbide 3.76–3.79 Å (b0027).

The N–W (Nishiyama–Wasserman) orientation relationship between κ-carbide and α matrix is found mainly between lamellar κ-carbide and α at 700 °C and is hardly found once the annealing temperature reaches 800 °C (and 850 °C) (b0047).

For the 850 °C specimen the work hardening rate is higher in the early stage (true strain < about 5%), being in the reverse order of the annealing temperatures, and decreases quickly to become lower than the 900 °C specimen in the later stage (b0035, b0063).
The actual dissolution temperature for κ-carbide with 1 h annealing is between 850 °C and 900 °C, higher than the Thermo-Calc value of about 823 °C (b0052, b0033).

In the Fe–Mn–Al–C steel comparison (Table 2), the present steel (855 MPa ultimate / 651 MPa yield / γ + α(40%) + boundary κ / 36.6% elongation / 31 GPa%) has the lowest ultimate elongation and lowest strength–ductility product of the set, attributed to the highest α phase fraction, boundary κ-carbide and inhomogeneous microstructure (b0071, table_002).
No obvious TRIP or TWIP phenomenon was found during the tensile test according to TEM examination of the deformed microstructure (b0040).

No obvious superlattice spots were seen in the SADPs of α or γ phase in the annealed specimens; ordering of atoms in α or γ is not expected during annealing at 700–1200 °C for 1 h, though ordering may occur during quenching (b0033).
